mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a risk-off sentiment that short-cuts expected corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (t-test p > 0.10) or the Fed rate does not revert below 5.25% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5%, it reflects accelerating inflation expectations that compress real discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in >70% of similar inflation spikes (rolling IC > 0.05) or inflation decelerates by >1.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 5,000 jobs signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥5,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of similar monthly payroll gains (rolling IC < -0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (billions of chained USD) grows by at least 10% over the prior quarter, it indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings momentum, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 over 12 months post-signal or earnings revisions turn negative in 70% of such quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO index below 100 (after normalization) indicates softening supply-side conditions that raise uncertainty and compress valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during similar supply shocks (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both HOUST (units) and RSAFS (dollars) for two consecutive months signals persistent demand across sectors, which tends to drive equity price appreciation over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of such interaction events (rolling IC < -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months, it indicates a labor market cooling that raises policy uncertainty and typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in >50% of similar cooling episodes (rolling IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4.0% for 3 months), the absence of a sharp yield curve steepening suggests continued accommodative policy that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% for 3 consecutive months and no sharp yield curve steepening
regime_hint: prolonged monetary easing without policy tightening signals
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >70% of similar easing periods (rolling IC < -0.20).
